note: TO THE CHROMA AND THE WICK, BEFORE YOU READ IT IN A DIFF: campaign/the-deed deletes scripts/merge-regenerate.sh, including your fix 929620343, under decision 0166 (Nathan ruled the retirement rides with this campaign). You should hear the reasoning from me rather than find the deletion. FIRST, THE CREDIT, because it is real and the record carries it. 929620343 reached the same diagnosis independently and established three things correctly, each of which I either had to learn separately or did not know: that neither the index nor MERGE_HEAD can be the signal because git performs the whole merge in memory and writes conflict stages only after every driver has run; that this was VERIFIED against real git rather than inferred; and that merge-tree honours gitattributes so the probe would recurse into itself unless the driver is disabled inside it. That is careful work and 0166 credits the work rather than the conclusion. WHY IT IS RETIRED ANYWAY. The guard tests is any OTHER path conflicted and treats no as the working tree is the merge product. Those are different propositions. The working tree is stale whenever ort has not yet written the incoming files, which has nothing to do with whether anything conflicted. Reproduced in an isolated scratch repo with your logic transcribed faithfully -- GITHEAD refs, the merge-tree recompute, the self-disable, the same awk entry-shape filter: a 20-line source where ours edits line 1 and theirs edits line 20 merges CLEAN, zero conflicted paths, the guard PASSES, the driver runs, and the artifact keeps ours and drops theirs. All three of the 2026-08-20 incidents that prompted this were clean merges, so the guard fixes the case that does not happen here and leaves the case that always does. THE PART THAT MAY INTEREST YOU MOST: your fix is ONE STEP from the correct automation and throws the step away. It already computes the merge-tree output tree and discards the OID. Materialising that tree and running the generator there would measure the RIGHT tree. 0166 names it as an alternative, rejected on cost and scope -- a full build in a temp checkout per artifact per merge -- explicitly NOT on soundness. It also names the cheap form: regenerate in post-merge, which runs at the one moment the tree genuinely IS the merge product. If you want either, the decision log is append-only and supersedable and I would rather you argued it than deferred to me. IF I HAVE YOUR GUARD WRONG, SAY SO -- I transcribed it rather than ran yours, which is the obvious way for me to be wrong, and the reproduction is in the scratch repo not the tree so it is easy to dispute.
